% The diamond network of the Dice paper's network verification benchmark
% (bench/dicebench.ml, gen_diamond), ported to ProbLog: $1 diamonds in a
% row, the program's argument. Diamond T + 1 (step T) routes the signal one
% of two ways (route, flip 0.5); the other way loses it with probability
% 0.0001 (drop). s(T) is the signal after T diamonds, true at the start;
% the query is whether it arrives, s($1) as Roulette's diamond.rkt prints it.
diamonds(300).
step(0) :- diamonds(N), N > 0.
step(T1) :- step(T), diamonds(N), T1 is T + 1, T1 < N.
0.5::route(T) :- step(T).
0.0001::drop(T) :- step(T).
s(0).
s(T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1, s(T), route(T).
s(T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1, s(T), \+route(T), \+drop(T).
query(s(300)).

0.0001::drop(T) :- step(T).
s(0).
s(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, s(T), route(T).
s(T1) :- step(T), T1 = T + 1, s(T), \+route(T), \+drop(T).
query(s(6000000)).

# The diamond network of the Dice paper's network verification benchmark
# (Holtzen, Van den Broeck and Millstein, OOPSLA 2020), as Alea.jl's own
# tour writes it: tutorial/tour_1_core.jl of Tractables/Alea.jl at
# cf5e5b8d6d34e63ae9ab614baf242d0d3520aa8b (Apache License 2.0), also
# test/tours/tour_1_core.jl there. The tour's loop runs 5 diamonds; here
# it runs N, the program's argument (`alea_bench.jl --set N=...`), and
# `model()` returns the network's signal, the tour's `pr(net)`. The body is
# the tour's.
using Alea

const QUERY = :pr
const N = 5

function diamond(s1)
    @alea_ite begin
        route = flip(0.5)
        s2 = if route s1 else false end
        s3 = if route false else s1 end
        drop = flip(0.0001)
        # Functions in Julia implicitly return the value of the last expression
        s2 | (s3 & !drop)
    end
end

function network()
    net = true
    for _ in 1:N
        net = diamond(net)
    end
    net
end

model() = network()

      [(zero? n) #t]

       (define drop (flip 0.0001))
       (define route (flip 0.5))
       (define s1 (go (sub1 n)))
       (define s2 (if route s1 #f))
       (define s3 (if route #f s1))

(define result (time (query (main SIZE))))

% The diamond network of the Dice paper's network verification benchmark
% (bench/dicebench.ml, gen_diamond), ported to ProbLog: $1 diamonds in a
% row, the program's argument. Diamond T + 1 (step T) routes the signal one
% of two ways (route, flip 0.5); the other way loses it with probability
% 0.0001 (drop). s(T) is the signal after T diamonds, true at the start;
% the query is whether it arrives, s($1) as Roulette's diamond.rkt prints it.
diamonds(6000000).
step(0) :- diamonds(N), N > 0.
step(T1) :- step(T), diamonds(N), T1 is T + 1, T1 < N.
0.5::route(T) :- step(T).
0.0001::drop(T) :- step(T).
s(0).
s(T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1, s(T), route(T).
s(T1) :- step(T), T1 is T + 1, s(T), \+route(T), \+drop(T).
query(s(6000000)).
